title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

file_summaries.semantic_summary:
- Overall data structure and type
  - Tabular (CSV) with one record per agent; agent_id is the unique key.
  - Columns:
    - Demographics: age (int), age_group (categorical), occupation (categorical).
    - Behavioral state/trait: initial_mask_wearing (bool), risk_perception (float in [0,1]).
    - Network degrees: family_connections, work_school_connections, community_connections (ints), and total_connections (int = sum of the three).
- Relationships or nested elements
  - No nested structures; flat schema.
  - No explicit edges are provided—only per-layer degree counts per agent.
  - Implies a multiplex network with three layers (family, work/school, community); total_connections is a derived field validating degree sums.
- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Agent initialization: create one agent per row with the given demographics, initial_mask_wearing state, and risk_perception trait.
  - Network construction: generate a three-layer (family, work/school, community) graph using the provided degree sequence per layer (e.g., configuration model), enforcing that each agent’s degree matches its counts; optionally apply assortativity/homophily by age_group and occupation when pairing stubs.
  - Interaction dynamics:
    - Use layer-specific contacts to compute social influence (e.g., fraction of masked neighbors per layer).
    - Weight layers differently (family > work/school > community, if desired).
    - Update mask adoption probability as a function of risk_perception and observed neighbor masking (and optionally demographics/occupation).
  - Validation: ensure degree sums are even per layer and total_connections equals the per-layer sum; handle missing/boolean parsing consistently.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json (for mask-wearing diffusion simulation)

- Overall data structure and type
  - JSON object (dictionary) keyed by agent IDs (as strings, e.g., "0", "1", …).
  - Each key maps to an object of adjacency lists (arrays of integers) representing social ties.
  - Static, unweighted network; IDs range up to ~999 (implies ~1,000 agents).

- Relationships or nested elements
  - Four neighbor lists per agent:
    - family: household/close-kin ties.
    - work_school: coworkers/classmates.
    - community: broader community contacts.
    - all: union of the above lists (deduplicated); order is not meaningful.
  - Edges are specified from the ego’s perspective; reciprocity is not guaranteed (may be directed in data; symmetrize if needed).
  - Multiplex structure: the same alter may appear in multiple layers (overlapping contexts).

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Agents: one per key (node). Store per-layer neighbor sets to preserve context.
  - Interaction scheduling: use layer-specific contact processes (e.g., higher frequency/weight for family, medium for work_school, lower for community). Alternatively, use all for an aggregated model.
  - Influence dynamics: apply layer-dependent influence strengths/probabilities (e.g., stronger conformity within family), or threshold models that aggregate signals across layers with weights.
  - Initialization/preprocessing:
    - Convert keys to ints; validate that referenced IDs exist; recompute all as union of the three layers if needed.
    - Decide on directed vs. undirected edges; if undirected is desired, symmetrize adjacency.
    - Optionally derive weights per layer or per-overlap (e.g., tie appears in multiple layers => stronger influence).
  - Metrics that may guide parameterization: degree per layer, overlap between layers, clustering; these affect adoption speed and cascade potential.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv

Overall data structure and type
- CSV in long (panel) format: one row per (agent_id, day).
- Columns:
  - day: integer, discrete timestep index.
  - agent_id: integer, unique agent identifier.
  - wearing_mask: boolean, agent’s behavioral state that day.
  - received_info: boolean, whether the agent received pro-mask information that day.
- Primary key: composite (agent_id, day). Flat records; no nesting.

Relationships or nested elements
- Temporal linkage within agent_id: ordered sequence across days forms a time series per agent.
- State dependence: wearing_mask at day t can depend on wearing_mask at t-1 and received_info at t.
- No explicit cross-agent relationships or network topology; social ties are not encoded here.
- received_info represents exogenous exposure events in this file; potential causal driver of behavior but not tied to a source.

How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
- Agent initialization: set each agent’s initial wearing_mask from day 0 (or earliest observed day).
- Behavioral dynamics calibration:
  - Estimate transition probabilities P(W_t | W_{t-1}, received_info_t) to parameterize daily update rules.
  - If multiple agents are present, estimate heterogeneity (agent-specific propensities or random effects).
  - Derive persistence/habit strength from switching rates (on→off, off→on).
- Information effects: quantify effect size of received_info on adoption probability; map this to messages from neighbors in the network model.
- Exogenous inputs: use received_info as shocks or seeding events in absence of network-driven exposure.
- Validation targets: match marginal adoption rates and transition matrices over time between simulation and observed data.
- Missing components for full social diffusion: network edges/topology and who-exposed-whom. If not provided, generate or import a network and define diffusion rules; use this file to calibrate individual response parameters. Note: sample snippet has received_info=false throughout, so estimating info effects requires rows where received_info=true.

overall_simulation_design.rationale: The goal is to simulate how mask-wearing behavior diffuses through social networks and assess the effect of interventions (e.g., targeted information, mandates, changing layer weights). The provided data support parameter calibration (train_data.csv), agent and network initialization (agent_attributes.csv, social_network.json), and scenario testing under alternative policies.
overall_simulation_design.initialization: 1) Load agent_attributes.csv to create one agent per row; set static demographics and traits; initialize wearing_mask from train_data day 0 when available else from initial_mask_wearing. 2) Load social_network.json to build multiplex edges (family, work_school, community); deduplicate per layer; optionally symmetrize. 3) Calibrate behavior parameters using train_data.csv transitions P(W_t | W_{t-1}, received_info_t) via logistic regression or frequency estimates; derive inertia and info effects. 4) Seed exogenous received_info schedules from train_data for the training horizon; for what-if periods, use scenario generators (e.g., campaign intensity).
outputs: Per-agent daily states: wearing_mask_t, received_info_t, perceived_neighbor_mask_fraction by layer
Aggregate adoption curves by day (overall and by age_group/occupation)
Layer-specific influence diagnostics (elasticities, effective reproduction of behavior Rb)
Transition matrices (P00, P01, P10, P11) simulated vs observed
Intervention impact reports (e.g., delta adoption at T, time-to-50% adoption)
Run logs with random seeds and parameter settings for reproducibility

scale_granularity.population_size: Number of unique agent_ids in social_network.json intersected with agent_attributes.csv (≈1,000)
scale_granularity.rationale: Behavior is observed daily in train_data.csv; no spatial coordinates are provided; the social network defines interaction structure over ~1,000 agents.

agent_archetypes.construction_from_data: For each row in agent_attributes.csv, create agent with given demographics and risk_perception. Initialize wearing_mask at day 0 using train_data.csv if present; otherwise use initial_mask_wearing. Degrees are stored for validation against social_network.json. Role is assigned from occupation (Student | Blue Collar | White Collar; else Other).
agent_archetypes.update_from_data: Estimate behavioral inertia and information effects from train_data.csv: compute empirical P01 (adopt), P11 (stay wearing), P10 (drop) conditional on received_info_t and W_{t-1}. Fit a logistic model P(W_t=1)=sigmoid(β0+βI*W_{t-1}+βinfo*received_info_t) on training days lacking network inputs; use these β as priors when adding network terms.

interaction_topology.construction_from_data: Parse social_network.json; convert keys to int. For each agent, store neighbor sets per layer and an 'all' union (deduplicated). Validate that neighbor counts approximate the counts in agent_attributes.csv; log discrepancies. Optionally symmetrize: if j in i.layer but i not in j.layer, add reciprocal with probability p_sym (calibratable). Overlapping ties across layers may be weighted more strongly.

information_propagation.topology: family, work_school, community layers (and their union for aggregated effects)
information_propagation.mechanism: Behavioral observation and social influence via weighted neighbor masking: each day, agents observe the fraction of masked neighbors per layer. Adoption probability follows a logistic or threshold rule combining inertia, layer-weighted neighbor fractions, risk_perception, and exogenous info. Optionally, informational messages propagate along edges at rate λ, increasing received_info_t.
information_propagation.construction_from_data: Layer edges and degrees from social_network.json. Baseline inertia and exogenous info effect from train_data.csv transitions. Risk_perception from agent_attributes.csv moderates susceptibility.

parameters.notes: Layer weights (w_*) scale perceived_mask_frac per layer. beta_* are logistic coefficients estimated from train_data and refined via calibration. lambda_info_edge sets probability that an informed neighbor triggers received_info_t. theta_threshold enables optional threshold adoption (activate if >0). overlap_boost scales ties appearing in multiple layers.

exogenous_signals.name: received_info_exogenous
exogenous_signals.construction_from_data: train_data.csv 'received_info' per (agent, day) where available; for counterfactual days, generate via a Bernoulli process with mean set by campaign_intensity
exogenous_signals.effect_on_agents: Adds β_info to the logistic score for adoption on day t; increments cumulative_info_exposures_t

exogenous_signals.name: mask_mandate_scenario
exogenous_signals.construction_from_data: scenario parameter (not present in files); can be set to 0 (none) to 1 (strong)
exogenous_signals.observability: global and immediate for all agents
exogenous_signals.effect_on_agents: Adds β_policy * mandate_level to the logistic score; optionally scales w_work upward to represent enforcement in workplaces/schools

Student.policy_form: Logistic: P(W_t=1)=sigmoid(β0_r + βI_r*W_{t-1} + wF_r*perc_family + wW_r*perc_work + wC_r*perc_comm + βrisk_r*risk_perception + βinfo_r*received_info_t + βpolicy_r*mandate)

Blue Collar.policy_form: Logistic with stronger work layer weight

White Collar.policy_form: Logistic with moderate work and community weights; potentially higher responsiveness to received_info

Other.policy_form: Logistic with family and community emphasis

holdout_plan.train_range: First 80% of days per agent (day 0 to floor(0.8*T_i)-1 for each agent i with T_i total observed days)
holdout_plan.validation_range: Last 20% of days per agent (day floor(0.8*T_i) to T_i-1)
holdout_plan.notes: Fit logistic coefficients on training days using only exogenous received_info and inertia where network masking is unobserved; then simulate forward on validation days using the network to produce perceived fractions and compare to observed wearing_mask. Optionally add a rolling-backtest for robustness.

metrics.name: RMSE_aggregate
metrics.definition: Root Mean Squared Error between simulated and observed daily mask adoption rates (overall and by subgroup) on validation days

metrics.name: MAE_aggregate
metrics.definition: Mean Absolute Error between simulated and observed adoption curves

metrics.name: Brier
metrics.definition: Average squared error between per-agent simulated P(W_t=1) and observed outcomes on validation days

metrics.name: TransitionFit
metrics.definition: Absolute/relative error between simulated and observed transition probabilities P01, P11, P10 over validation

simulation_evaluation.comparison_method: Compute per-day and subgroup adoption rates from validation ground truth (train_data.csv). Run N stochastic simulations per parameter set; average metrics across runs with confidence intervals. Report tables of metrics and plots of observed vs simulated curves and transition matrices.

calibratable_parameters.name: w_family
calibratable_parameters.source: Layer influence strength; constrained by family layer edges and observed adoption dynamics
calibratable_parameters.notes: Higher values increase conformity to family masking

calibratable_parameters.name: beta_inertia
calibratable_parameters.source: Estimated from P(W_t | W_{t-1}) in train_data

calibratable_parameters.name: beta_risk
calibratable_parameters.notes: Positive if higher risk increases adoption

calibratable_parameters.name: beta_info
calibratable_parameters.notes: Maps exogenous info to adoption likelihood

calibratable_parameters.name: lambda_info_edge
calibratable_parameters.source: Rate that informed neighbors transmit info
calibratable_parameters.notes: Supports endogenous info diffusion if enabled

calibratable_parameters.name: theta_threshold
calibratable_parameters.source: Optional adoption threshold on weighted neighbor fraction
calibratable_parameters.notes: If 0, pure logistic; if >0, add threshold effect

calibratable_parameters.name: overlap_boost
calibratable_parameters.source: Strength multiplier for ties appearing in multiple layers

calibratable_parameters.name: p_sym
calibratable_parameters.source: Probability to add reciprocal edges when symmetrizing the network

calibratable_parameters.name: memory_decay
calibratable_parameters.source: Decay of perceived neighbor masking over time
